SNG.P.3.6-11.text: Solomon Arrives on His Wedding Day

SNG.1.1-4.text: The bride longs for her beloved’s kisses and love

SNG.1.5-6.text: The bride says she is dark but lovely

SNG.1.7-7.text: The bride asks where her beloved feeds his sheep

SNG.1.8-8.text: The bride is told to follow the flock’s tracks

SNG.1.9-11.text: The bridegroom compares the bride to a mare

SNG.1.12-14.text: The bride compares her beloved to sweet perfume

SNG.1.15-15.text: The bridegroom tells the bride she is beautiful

SNG.1.16-17.text: The bride praises her beloved and the grass bed

SNG.2.1-2.text: The bridegroom says the bride is a lily among thorns

SNG.2.3-4.text: The bride says her beloved is like an apple tree

SNG.2.5-6.text: The bride is faint with love and held by her beloved

SNG.2.7-7.text: The bride asks the women of Jerusalem not to rush love

SNG.2.8-9.text: The bride sees her beloved coming like a gazelle

SNG.2.10-11.text: The beloved calls the bride to come away; winter is past

SNG.2.12-13.text: The beloved says spring has come and calls the bride

SNG.2.14-14.text: The beloved asks the bride to show her face and voice

SNG.2.15-15.text: The lovers ask for the little foxes to be caught

SNG.2.16-17.text: The bride says she and her beloved belong to each other

SNG.3.1-2.text: The bride searches the city at night for her beloved

SNG.3.3-4.text: The bride finds her beloved and holds him

SNG.3.5-5.text: The bride again asks Jerusalem’s women not to rush love

SNG.3.6-7.text: Solomon’s carriage comes from the wilderness with guards

SNG.3.8-9.text: Skilled men guard Solomon’s carriage made of Lebanon wood

SNG.3.10-11.text: The women of Zion are told to look at King Solomon

SNG.4.1-1.text: Solomon praises his bride’s eyes and hair

SNG.4.3-3.text: Solomon praises his bride’s lips, mouth and brow

SNG.4.4-5.text: Solomon praises his bride’s neck and breasts

SNG.4.6-7.text: Solomon tells his bride she is altogether beautiful

SNG.4.8-8.text: Solomon calls his bride to come away from Lebanon

SNG.4.9-9.text: Solomon says his bride has captured his heart

SNG.4.10-11.text: Solomon says his bride’s love is better than wine

SNG.4.12-14.text: Solomon calls his bride a locked garden full of spices

SNG.4.15-16.text: The bride invites Solomon to come into his garden

SNG.5.1-1.text: Solomon enjoys his garden and invites friends to eat

SNG.5.2-2.text: The bride hears her beloved knocking at night

SNG.5.3-4.text: The bride hesitates to get up for her beloved

SNG.5.5-5.text: The bride rises to open the door for her beloved

SNG.5.6-6.text: The bride opens the door, but her beloved is gone

SNG.5.7-7.text: The watchmen beat the bride in the city

SNG.5.8-8.text: The bride asks the women of Jerusalem to find her beloved

SNG.5.9-9.text: The women ask the bride why her beloved is special

SNG.5.10-11.text: The bride praises her beloved’s head and hair

SNG.5.12-12.text: The bride praises her beloved’s eyes

SNG.5.13-13.text: The bride praises her beloved’s cheeks and lips

SNG.5.14-14.text: The bride praises her beloved’s arms and body

SNG.5.15-15.text: The bride praises her beloved’s legs and appearance

SNG.5.16-16.text: The bride says her beloved is altogether lovely

SNG.6.1-1.text: The women ask where the bride’s beloved has gone

SNG.6.2-3.text: The bride says her beloved is in his garden

SNG.6.4-4.text: Solomon says his bride is beautiful and majestic

SNG.6.5-5.text: Solomon says his bride’s eyes have overcome him

SNG.6.6-7.text: The man praises the woman’s teeth and brow

SNG.6.8-9.text: The man says the woman is more special than queens

SNG.6.10-10.text: Others praise the woman as bright as sun and moon

SNG.6.11-12.text: The woman goes to the walnut grove to see the blossoms

SNG.6.13-13.text: Friends call the Shulammite woman to come back

SNG.7.1-1.text: The man praises the woman’s feet and thighs

SNG.7.2-2.text: The man praises the woman’s navel and waist

SNG.7.3-4.text: The man praises the woman’s neck, eyes and nose

SNG.7.5-6.text: The man praises the woman’s head, hair and delights

SNG.7.7-8.text: The man compares the woman to a palm tree

SNG.7.9-9.text: The man says the woman’s mouth is like fine wine

SNG.7.10-11.text: The woman invites the man to go to the countryside

SNG.7.12-12.text: The woman invites the man to the vineyards for love

SNG.7.13-13.text: The woman has fine fruits and gifts for the man

SNG.8.1-1.text: The woman wishes the man were like a brother

SNG.8.2-3.text: The woman wants to bring the man to her mother’s house

SNG.8.4-4.text: The woman asks the daughters of Jerusalem not to rush love

SNG.8.5-5.text: Others see the woman coming up leaning on the man

SNG.8.6-6.text: The woman says love is as strong as death

SNG.8.7-7.text: Water cannot put out love, and wealth cannot buy it

SNG.8.8-8.text: The brothers ask what to do for the little sister

SNG.8.9-9.text: The brothers plan to protect the little sister

SNG.8.10-10.text: The woman says she is a wall and has found peace

SNG.8.11-12.text: The woman says her own vineyard is hers to give

SNG.8.13-13.text: The man asks the woman to let him hear her voice

SNG.8.14-14.text: The woman calls the man to come away like a gazelle
